prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Conservative Party Manifesto 2017 – Summary (under 500 words)

Vision and context
- Calls for “strong and stable” leadership to deliver a smooth, orderly Brexit and tackle five giant challenges: a strong economy; Brexit in a changing world; enduring social divisions; an ageing society; and fast-changing technology.
- Governing from the mainstream: active, pragmatic government to make markets work for everyone and build a “Great Meritocracy.”

Economy and business
- Sound public finances with a balanced budget by mid-2020s; keep taxes as low as possible; no VAT rise; raise personal allowance to £12,500 and higher rate to £50,000 by 2020.
- Cut Corporation Tax to 17% by 2020; reform business rates; simplify tax.
- Trade: deep and special UK–EU partnership; new global trade deals; revive Board of Trade; UK Export Finance at the core.
- Corporate governance: annual binding votes on executive pay, publish pay ratios, curb abusive share buybacks; employee voice on boards via one of three routes.
- Worker rights: raise National Living Wage to 60% of median by 2020 then by median earnings; act on gig economy protections (post-Taylor Review).
- Tackle tax avoidance/evasion; strengthen pensions regulator powers.
- Modern Industrial Strategy: raise R&D to 2.4% of GDP within 10 years (goal 3%); Institutes of Technology; £23bn National Productivity Investment Fund; Future Britain sovereign funds.
- Energy: independent review to cut costs; safeguard tariff cap for households; diverse mix (offshore wind, shale with new regulator); industrial energy efficiency scheme.

Infrastructure and regions
- Invest in HS2, Northern Powerhouse Rail, Heathrow, roads, EVs and charging, rail capacity; expand cycle networks.
- Spread prosperity: devolve and relocate government/cultural bodies; support city deals; coastal and rural support; farming transition post-CAP; 25-year Environment Plan; CCTV in slaughterhouses; consider ending live export for slaughter.

Brexit and the Union
- Leave single market and customs union; Great Repeal Bill to convert EU law; no EU Charter of Fundamental Rights; ECHR retained next parliament.
- Protect Common Travel Area; aim for frictionless NI/ROI border; vote on final deal in Parliament.
- United Kingdom Shared Prosperity Fund to replace EU structural funds.
- Oppose a second Scottish independence referendum “now.”

Security, defence, and justice
- Defence: meet NATO 2% and rise 0.5% above inflation annually; renew Trident; £178bn equipment plan; support veterans.
- Counter-terrorism, cyber security investment; merge SFO into NCA; create national infrastructure police.
- Prisons: 10,000 new places; focus on safety, work, rehabilitation; tougher community sentences; women’s provision.
- Democracy: boundary review to 600 MPs; ID to vote; repeal Fixed-term Parliaments Act; retain first-past-the-post.

Meritocracy: education, skills, work
- Create more good school places: 100+ free schools/year; lift ban on new selective schools with conditions; widen university/independent school sponsorship; specialist maths schools.
- Curriculum: EBacc expansion; stronger literacy/numeracy; reduce teaching-to-test.
- Funding: fairer formula, no school loses cash; extra £4bn by 2022; replace universal infant lunches with universal breakfasts; protect Pupil Premium.
- Technical education: T-levels, longer courses, mandatory work placements; Institutes of Technology; 3m apprenticeships by 2020; discounted travel for apprentices; career-long retraining.
- Immigration: reduce net migration to tens of thousands; tougher student/family visas; align skills visas with industrial strategy; double Immigration Skills Charge; integration strategy; counter extremism with new commission.

Social justice and cost of living
- Close gender pay gap; race disparity audit actions; disability employment up by 1m; new Mental Health Bill; 10,000 more MH staff; workplace MH first aid.
- Domestic Violence and Abuse Bill; rough sleeping halved then ended by 2027 (Housing First pilots).
- Consumer markets: stronger regulators; fair rail ticketing and ombudsman; tackle rogue parking; telecoms billing fairness; cap energy standard tariffs; smart meters for all by 2020.

Pensions, social care, NHS, housing, families
- Pensions: Triple Lock to 2020 then Double Lock; state pension age to reflect longevity; expand auto-enrolment, Lifetime ISA.
- Social care: include home value in means-test for home/residential care; £100k asset floor; deferred payments extended to domiciliary care; means-test Winter Fuel Payments; green paper on quality/integration.
- NHS: at least £8bn real-terms rise over 5 years; more UK-trained doctors; invest in buildings/tech; recover costs from non-residents; faster access to innovation; seven-day services; retain A&E 95% and 18-week targets; cancer 28-day diagnosis; expand dentistry/community pharmacy; major mental health expansion.
- Housing: 1.5m homes by 2022; protect Green Belt; better design/infrastructure; council housing deals for fixed-term social homes with RTB; empower housing associations; capture land value; £2.5bn flood defences.
- Childcare: 30 free hours for 3–4s; expand nursery places (school-based); youth mental health reforms.

Digital age
- Digital Charter: best place to start/run digital businesses and safest online; new data protection law; data rights (including deletion at 18); Data Use and Ethics Commission.
- Full-fibre spines, gigabit rollout, 95% geographic mobile coverage by 2022; 5G majority coverage by 2027; easier switching.
- Online safety: stronger platform duties, counter-terror content removal, protections for children; potential levy on platforms; stronger cyber standards.
- Digital government by default; Verify ID; open data; geospatial data body combining land/mapping functions.

International
- Maintain 0.7% aid with stricter rules; lead on climate action, modern slavery, girls’ education; reform asylum to focus on most in need overseas.
